title: "Derive outcomes, comorbidities, and costs"
output: rmarkdown::html_document

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The examples use invented data.

## Add outcomes and score comorbidities

> The NIS has no diagnosis-level present-on-admission fields (`DXPOA`).
> The default Elixhauser method assumes diagnoses were present on admission.
> That assumption differs from the AHRQ Refined method with known POA.
> Document it if you use these scores for risk adjustment.

```{r outcomes}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
outcomes <- nis |> nis_outcomes()
outcomes |> count(in_hospital_death) |> collect()
```

`DIED` defines in-hospital death. `DISPUNIFORM` describes where the patient
went at discharge. `los_days` comes from `LOS`. Keep all three source fields
when calling `nis_outcomes()`.

Install `medicalcoder` to run this Charlson example. Expect a warning
about absent present-on-admission fields. The method assumes the
diagnoses were present on admission.

```{r comorbidity}
scored <- outcomes |> nis_comorbidity(method = "charlson_quan2005")
scored |> count(cmrb_n) |> arrange(cmrb_n) |> collect()
```

Score before `nis_design()` while the diagnosis slots are available and
DuckDB can still apply the mappings. Choose the method and code system for
your study period. The bundled `"elixhauser_ahrq2027"` method has no `medicalcoder` dependency.

Set `count_distinct = TRUE` to add the integer column `cmrb_n_distinct`.
The distinct count counts each condition represented by the output flags once.
For example, the refined Elixhauser flag for hypertension with heart failure
and severe renal failure represents three conditions, even when separate
flags for those conditions are also true. Diabetes and other severity
variants of the same condition share an ID. `cmrb_n` still reports the
method's own category count.

```{r distinct-comorbidities}
method <- "elixhauser_ahrq2027"
condition_map <- nis_comorbidity_condition_map(method)
condition_map |> filter(condition == "diabetes")

outcomes |>
  nis_comorbidity(method, count_distinct = TRUE, exclude_conditions = "diabetes") |>
  count(cmrb_n, cmrb_n_distinct) |>
  arrange(cmrb_n, cmrb_n_distinct) |>
  collect()
```

Use IDs from the map to exclude conditions that your analysis handles
separately. The count uses the flags emitted by the chosen method and
inherits their present-on-admission assumptions. Exclusions affect only the
distinct count. A discharge without usable codes has a missing count, and a
discharge with usable codes and no included conditions has a count of zero.

## Estimate costs in a common dollar year

```{r cost}
charges <- outcomes |> select(YEAR, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS) |> collect()
costs <- nis_cost(charges, dollars = 2020)
nis_cost_provenance(costs)$multipliers
costs |>
  summarise(mean_charge = mean(charges_adj), mean_cost = mean(cost_adj), .by = YEAR)
```

Join the year-specific HCUP cost-to-charge ratio before estimating costs
if the data lack `CCR_NIS`. `charges_adj` is the adjusted billed amount.
`cost_adj` applies the hospital ratio to estimate costs. Missing or invalid
ratios yield missing costs. CPI-U tracks general consumer price inflation.
It does not track hospital-specific input prices. When comparing with a
legacy result, check its charge field, CCR source, price index, and
dollar year. Keep the provenance alongside both cost and charge results.
The means here describe the invented sample. Use the survey design for
national estimates.
[Years and coding eras](years-and-eras.html)

If `nis_design()` keeps both `TOTCHG` and `CCR_NIS`, it adds `charges_adj` and
`cost_adj` in dollars of the latest included year by default. Use `nis_cost()`
to set a common dollar year across separate analyses and retain the
provenance with your results.
